posts.text: Yemeni gov’t forces, Houthis trade blame for deadly strikes on Taiz market — The attack on al-Hadara market in Taiz governorate's al-Waziiya district killed at least 30 people, Houthi rebels say.

Pro-Israel Republican makes major campaign finance pledge after razor-thin election victory — Anna Paulina Luna says she will reject all corporate PAC money and foreign policy-linked funding after her narrow midterm victory in Florida.
Swings in Farm Areas Helped Propel Democrats to Victory — Anger over tariffs and higher costs because of the war in Iran led many Republican farmers and ranchers to vote blue — or stay home.

Russia secretly bolstered Iran's missile arsenal before war with US, records uncover — Internal Russian defense documents reveal a contract for 90 precision-guided missile launchers destined for Iran, detailing Moscow's military support.

Reporter's Notebook: How midterms may change the House impeachment equation for Hegseth — Thomas Massie plans to reintroduce articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth next week, and post-midterm GOP math could work against the Pentagon chief.

Europe Still Sees Trump As Powerful, Especially in Foreign Policy — The commanding victory of the Democrats has brought private relief to some Europeans but no official glee, with Ukraine, Iran and NATO all hanging in the balance.

Bitter Fetterman-El-Sayed feud threatens to complicate Schumer's Senate unity push — Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer's Party unity push faces an early test as John Fetterman and Abdul El-Sayed trade insults over U.S. aid to Israel.

'He's got to go': Hakeem Jeffries calls for Hegseth's removal but stops short of impeachment — Speaking with Morning Edition , Hakeem Jeffries discussed ending the Iran war, holding Trump accountable and calls for new Democratic leadership, but offered few specifics on how Democrats would deliver.
